title: Procedural DNA Double Helix Unzip
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D educational scene of a DNA double helix that can be unzipped. Use Three.js (via CDN) and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Dark navy background (0x0a0a2e).
- Perspective camera at position (0, 5, 25), looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.5) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) from (10, 20, 10).
- OrbitControls for camera rotation/zoom.

## DNA Double Helix Construction
- Procedurally generate a DNA double helix along the Y-axis, from y = -12 to y = 12.
- Use 24 base pairs total, evenly spaced (1 unit apart along Y).
- Each base pair consists of:
  - Two backbone spheres (radius 0.3) on the left and right strands, colored blue (0x4488ff) for strand A and red (0xff4444) for strand B.
  - Backbone spheres follow a helix: for pair i, angle = i * (Math.PI / 6). Strand A: x = 3*cos(angle), z = 3*sin(angle). Strand B: x = 3*cos(angle + Math.PI), z = 3*sin(angle + Math.PI). y = -12 + i * 1.0.
  - A cylindrical bond (hydrogen bond) connecting the two backbone spheres of each pair, colored green (0x44ff88), radius 0.08.
  - Thin tube/cylinder segments connecting consecutive backbone spheres on each strand (sugar-phosphate backbone), colored matching the strand.
- Group all base pair elements so each pair can be individually manipulated.

## Duck.glb Asset (Helicase Enzyme)
- Load 'Duck.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to 0.015 so it's small. This represents the 'helicase enzyme' that unzips DNA.
- Position it initially at y = -12 (bottom of the helix), x = 0, z = 0.
- Rotate it so it faces upward along the Y-axis.
- The duck should be visible and labeled via a floating HTML label 'Helicase' near it.

## Unzipping Mechanics
- When the user clicks the 'Start Unzip' button, the duck (helicase) begins moving upward along y at a speed of 2 units per second.
- As the duck's y-position passes each base pair's y-position, that base pair 'unzips':
  - The green hydrogen bond cylinder fades out and is removed/hidden.
  - Strand A's backbone sphere for that pair moves outward (x += 2 in its local radial direction).
  - Strand B's backbone sphere moves outward in the opposite direction.
  - This creates a visible separation/fork.
- The unzip animation for each pair takes 0.5 seconds.
- A 'Pause' button toggles pause/resume of the unzipping.
- A 'Reset' button resets everything to initial state.

## Speed Control
- A slider (range input) labeled 'Speed' controls unzip speed from 0.5 to 5.0 units/sec (default 2.0).

## HUD / UI
- Top-left overlay div with:
  - Title: 'DNA Helicase Unzipping'
  - 'Pairs Unzipped: X / 24' counter
  - 'Helicase Position Y: XX.X'
  - 'Start Unzip' button (id='btn-start')
  - 'Pause' button (id='btn-pause')
  - 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset')
  - Speed slider (id='slider-speed')
- Style buttons with padding, border-radius, and readable fonts.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- helicaseY: current y-position of the duck (number)
- pairsUnzipped: number of base pairs fully unzipped (0-24)
- totalPairs: 24
- isUnzipping: boolean, true when animation is running
- isPaused: boolean
- speed: current speed value
- duckLoaded: boolean, true once Duck.glb is loaded
- unzipComplete: boolean, true when all 24 pairs are unzipped
- basePairStates: array of 24 values, each 'bonded' or 'unzipped'
- helicaseVisible: boolean

## Additional Details
- Add a subtle rotation animation to the entire helix (rotate around Y at 0.1 rad/s) when NOT unzipping.
- When unzipping starts, stop the idle rotation.
- After all pairs are unzipped, display 'Replication Fork Complete!' text in the HUD.
- Ensure no NaN values in any positions or state fields.
- The scene should be responsive to window resize.
physics_constraints: Helicase moves at configurable constant speed along Y-axis. Base pairs unzip sequentially as helicase passes them. Separation animation is smooth over 0.5s. No physics simulation needed but positions must remain NaN-free and bounded within scene limits.
